# Experiment results (generated by scripts/analyze.py)

## Experiment 3 - abrupt departures from 1000 nodes

k = 10, alpha = 3; 10 seeds per fraction, 100 node lookups and 50 distinct value lookups per seed. Healthy join/store precedes random abrupt removals. There are no arrivals, packet loss, real timeout delays or periodic maintenance during measurement. Each value reader is a live non-holder. This is a crash-fraction sweep, not a measured continuous churn rate.

| crashed | alive | closest live node found | value found | value has live copy | routing misses with live copy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% | 1000 | 1000/1000 | 500/500 | 500/500 | 0 |
| 10% | 900 | 1000/1000 | 500/500 | 500/500 | 0 |
| 30% | 700 | 1000/1000 | 500/500 | 500/500 | 0 |
| 50% | 500 | 1000/1000 | 500/500 | 500/500 | 0 |
| 80% | 200 | 848/1000 | 397/500 | 446/500 | 49 |
| 90% | 100 | 415/1000 | 201/500 | 316/500 | 115 |

Repair sources are selected from original surviving holders before reads, one per retained key, deduplicated by node. Each selected node calls Republish once after the lookup workload. Reads cache immutable values, so post-repair copy counts include caches and can exceed k. Placement is checked against the globally closest live k, independently of the routing tables.

| crashed | copies immediately after crash (all keys) | copies after repair (retained keys) | copies at true closest k after repair (retained keys) | retained keys restored at all k closest |

Join failures: 0; manual repair errors: 0. Data: `churn.jsonl`, `churn_runs.csv`, `churn.csv`. Figures: `churn_cost.svg`, `churn_availability.svg`, `churn_replicas.svg`.
